about: Coordinates measured from Yan Flash diagrams for drawing. Kept separate from the approved text data. Units: arena radius = 1, origin = arena centre, +x east, +y north. Every number here is derived from an image (never invented) and needs owner approval per scene.

measurement.base: Yan 2000x2000 diagrams share one arena: centre (1000,1000) px, playable edge radius 975 px (inside a ~20 px rim). Measured on yan-p1-06, -09, -12.

methods.auto: Role icon detected by colour (scripts/measure_yan.py); icon centre.
methods.eye: Read by eye from a 1000 px view (±0.01). Used for overlapping or faded icons.
methods.copy: Taken from another measured point, as noted.

waymarks.note: Same values in all three images (±0.006).

statue.note: P1 statue sits on the north rim in every P1 diagram.

arrowDrops.note: Your tile cell for this example arrow pair (Yan's tile layout, yan-p1-17). The arrow drops where you stand when its timer runs out.

p1-tele-trouncing/arrows.note: Example deal of arrow pairs, taken from Yan's status-bar screenshot (yan-p1-16): rows 2–5 (two different arrows) are read as MT, OT, H1, H2 and the four same-arrow rows as DPS, assuming the game's usual party-list order with your own row first. Which role gets the matching pairs, and who gets which pair, is random each pull (Azurite video 8:10). Debuffs go out when the Tele-trouncing cast ends (2:31.5, first step: nobody moves yet, owner round 10); the short-timer arrows drop at 2:39.4 and the long-timer ones at 2:42.4 (cactbot). With the same arrow twice, either cell can come first (Azurite video). The trap holders H2 and D4 match the 10 s debuff rows in the same screenshot.

carry.note: The debuffs go out while everyone still stands where Hyperdrive #2 left them: read your arrows, then walk to your frame.
